pages.text: I know now where the glow comes from. Roots. They hang from the ceiling of this cave like the veins of something enormous, thick and warm and slowly pulsing, and they do not end here. They run beneath everything, under every forest, under every mountain, under the very ground I have been sleeping on. The light does not come from the plants. The plants only drink it. I put my hand on one of the roots, and I felt a heartbeat. Slow, patient, much older than me. And for a moment it felt as if something on the other side of the bark had put its hand against mine as well.
